transferRevision: Emphasize chatting with a larger 66 by 26 px active-blue speech plate and 14 px dark text; temporarily hide the adjacent A label to prevent overlap. Character movement speeds up from 667 to 550 ms. Msg preparation and gathering slow slightly from 350 to 400 ms, and output copies slow slightly from 300 to 350 ms in both panels. Message sequence, receiving-sector selection, component positions and Digest sizing are unchanged.
composition: Before is above after; both panels occupy the full available width. At desktop widths the approved left-to-right sector / Msg or Digest / SendQ flow is preserved. Panels are never halved to place before and after in adjacent columns. Small mobile widths retain the established responsive flow without shrinking labels.
animation: Before runs first while after is inactive gray; after then runs while before is inactive gray. A starts bottom left, moves north in 550 ms, faces front and shows an emphasized chat bubble for the existing 850 ms chat phase, then moves east in 550 ms. Msg gathering takes 400 ms, output copies move in 350 ms, and after SendQ arrival remains visible for 650 ms.
rules: The same logical Msg IDs, bytes and per-recipient order are delivered before and after
Before loops around eligible recipients for each Msg
After retains source-sector packets, rebuilds the temporary Digest per receiving sector, then enqueues once per resident
The displayed recipient Msg badges are pending-send previews, not storage relocation
Each displayed receiving sector has one representative resident
Msg 1 and 2 originate in sector 3, which is in S1 and S2 neighborhoods; Msg 3 originates in sector 4, which is in all three neighborhoods
No new wire-level header is added by Digest

codeEvidence.afterEnqueue: RequestSendRaw after neighbor Msg byte concatenation

limits: Allocation, RefCount, actual WSASend execution, membership digest and global cleanup are omitted
The 3x3 map is a viewport, not a complete boundary for all recipient neighborhoods
The visualization starts from three logical Msgs; it does not depict dirty-move production, tick timing or membership-change packet creation
